claims.text: Sleep-deprived mice required 41 ± 6 trials to criterion after reversal versus 27 ± 4 for rested controls (n = 16 per group; d = 1.1; p < 0.001).
c-Fos-positive cell density in lateral orbitofrontal cortex did not differ between groups (312 ± 40 vs 298 ± 45 cells/mm²; p = 0.61).

Acute sleep deprivation impairs reversal learning without a detectable reduction in orbitofrontal activation, so the behavioural effect is unlikely to be mediated by lower orbitofrontal activity as measured here.
